[Opinion]My Take On Whether The Ralph Retort and Related Entities Should Be Censored

He's an asshole, but even an asshole has the right to say what they want to. We also have the right to hit ctrl+w and ignore what he says. What happened to "Sticks and stones may break my bones, but words will never hurt me." as a way to handle things? Ruining people's lives over a few harmless words is pointless. It's only when previous actions back their words and promise new and equally or more dangerous actions where words can be a problem, but even then the words act as an indicator rather than a direct deliverance of harm.

...Why are we even having this conversation? I know you and I have had our grinding points on opinion before, /u/GethN7 , but when a movement founded on media ethics watchdog'ism and anti-censorship begins asking itself whether it should censor people, then that movement, and especially those pushing said policy, seriously need to step back and take a look at what they're proposing.

Ralph has his right to say what he wants. If we don't like it, it's our right not to listen. The concept of Free Speech is as simple as that. That anyone that calls themself a part of GG and claim to respect the principles that originally bound us together would even think of proposing that we go the SJW route of censoring him for his unpopular beliefs and opinions, much less that they propose we do so, as a movement, sends waves of disgust at the utter and shameless hypocrisy shuddering down my spine.

GamerGate/KiA/etc needs to step back and really re-evaluate their agenda, as a whole. Are we still the media watchdogs clamoring for freedom of speech and freedom of the press we were when all of this shitstorm started? Or have we simply morphed into yet another version of SJW-Lite, perfectly okay with censoring the work of others, when it suits our politics? As I implied earlier, we shouldn't even need to be asking this question of whether or not to censor...the fact that we now are, speaks volumes and points to serious decay of core movement values below the surface.

As I stated in the article. my answer on censorship is a definite NO, except as regards to curtailing anything illegal. For the most part, I believe Ralph's speech is inflammatory yet legal, so censorship is, for the most part, unwarranted.

I acknowledge that, and my comments on our previous disagreement were meant to point out that past conflict as a way of contrasting my current position. My apologies, if I did not make myself sufficiently clear, on that. We are in agreement on the validity of Ralph's censorship, though I would go one step further to say it is more than unwarranted, it is despicable, considering who the calls for said censorship are coming from and what they allegedly stand for. I've been watching these elements slowly grow within GG for some time, and while I've spoken out against them, where I've seen them. What have we been fighting for, if we then turn around and embrace the same tactics and means our opposition is infamous for?

GG/KiA/etc is quickly approaching a moral horizon event where they will have to decide on what side of the issues they stand, Personal Liberty or the alluring yet destructive cause of Authoritarianism. What their collective answer turns out to be will influence my, and probably many others, answer as to whether or not to stick with GG/KiA/etc.

It's one of the reasons I have decided to disengage from taking a side and just give the whole thing a wide berth. Ralph and his associates may be inflammatory, but until they violate the law (and I don't believe I have the standing to make definitive judgements, only law enforcement does), who am I or anyone else to give them grief, and since I really have no dog in this fight nor wish to have one, I'm leaving both sides be.
